listing_view.reasoning: Demand built late but exploded on the final day to roughly 17.9x subscription (from ~1.28x on 2026-09-10 to 17.9x by 2026-09-11), which typically signals a hot listing regardless of fundamentals. I cannot verify the offer structure — the fresh issue figure exceeds the total issue size and the sources conflict — so pricing comfort is unverifiable; the score rests almost entirely on observed demand.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue is compounding at ~30% with 90.72% repeat orders and healthy cash conversion (~1.2x EBITDA), which is genuinely good. But EBITDA margin has compressed from 23.45% to 16.99%, leverage is high (debt/equity 1.57-1.77, and my own sum of the balance sheet gives 1.94 against the document's printed 1.57), the current ratio is a thin 0.36, and coal is a primary fuel — margin at the mercy of fuel costs they don't control.

governance.reasoning: 76% of total paid-up capital was pledged by the promoter against the company's debentures, with release confirmed only by email and conditional on full repayment, plus a SEBI rejection of an exemption application and a GPCB show cause notice.

key_risks.why_it_matters: 76% of paid-up capital was pledged to debenture trustees and must be re-pledged if the Ascertis debt is not fully repaid — a forced-sale or control risk hanging over minority investors.
EBITDA margin fell from 23.45% to 16.99% over two years while coal — a volatile input — is the primary fuel, so the growth is being bought at deteriorating unit economics.
Debt-to-equity is 1.57-1.77 (and my own calculation suggests 1.94), with a current ratio of just 0.36, meaning short-term liabilities are nearly three times short-term assets.
The top ten customers are 47.87% of revenue, so losing one or two contracts materially dents the growth story.
SEBI rejected an exemption application and the Gujarat Pollution Control Board issued a show cause notice — not disqualifying, but a pattern worth noting given the waste-fuel operations.
